newsitem.title: USA: Northeast says will pay nuke fine.
newsitem.headline: Northeast says will pay nuke fine.

text.p: Northeast Utilities said Monday it will pay a $650,000 fine proposed by federal regulators for past violations at its Connecticut Yankee nuclear power plant in Haddam Neck, Conn.
"We will pay the fine," a Northeast spokeswoman told Reuters.

The federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said earlier on Monday that it was citing Northeast for alleged violations of more than 70 agency requirements uncovered between November 1995 and November 1996.
Northeast had 30 days to pay the proposed fine or request in writing that all or part of the penalty be withdrawn.
The Connecticut Yankee plant was shut down last July for safety reasons, and Northeast announced last December that it would permanently close the facility.

"We have acknowledged the problems that led to these violations, and have made significant leadership changes as a result," Connecticut Yankee Chief Nuclear Officer Ted Feigenbaum said in a statement.

Among the changes were a new leadership team, an organization that was now "fully focused" on correcting problems, and upgraded procedures and programs to reflect a plant in permanent shutdown status, he said.
"We are determined to restore CY to its stature as a well-run facility and good neighbor," Feigenbaum said.
The 582-megawatt Connecticut Yankee was 49 percent owned by Northeast, with the balance owned by seven other New England utilities.
Northeast has said that Connecticut Yankee's dismantling will cost about $425 million.
